transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (CSM), Jordan (SE); Dr. Alicia Navarro, Ethan Brooks, Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor (Sunset Clinic)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff for Sunset Clinic to review scope of pilot, security/compliance needs, technical integration path (hosted API vs dedicated/private), and next steps to get the trial started.

Topics:
- Pilot goals and success criteria
- Integration options: hosted API, dedicated capacity, private VPC
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/encryption, data residency
- Technical checklist: API keys, sandbox, latency benchmarks, batching/caching configs
- Rollout and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick things off. Uh hi Alicia, Ethan, Priya, Liam — thanks for making time. We're going to run through a quick agenda, confirm pilot goals, and then Jordan will go over the technical plan.

[00:23] Dr. Alicia Navarro: Thanks Samira, yes excited to get started. We're trying to reduce clinician documentation time by about 25% in the pilot, and we need to make sure PHI is handled appropriately.

[00:40] Ethan Brooks: Hey, quick note on our side — we have an internal throughput target of around 60 QPS for the triage flow during peak, with p95 latency under 300ms ideally. Open to compromising on latency if costs blow up, but want to understand tradeoffs.

[01:05] Priya Singh: And from security, we need to know about data residency, encryption at rest/in transit, audit logs, SSO via SAML, and whether Redwood will be in our VPC or if we use hosted. We'll need SOC 2 as well.

[01:30] Samira: Yep all very fair. To summarize, for pilot we commonly run a hosted API first to get fast time-to-value, then move to Dedicated or Private if you need VPC or on-prem for PHI. We do support private deployments and customer-managed KMS. Jordan, do you want to walk through the technical integration options?

[01:50] Jordan Li (SE): Sure. So we usually start with a Redwood sandbox — we'll provision API keys and a test model. For production we offer three patterns: hosted (our managed API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), and Private (VPC / on-prem). The key tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to launch but you give us endpoint access; Dedicated gives predictable latency and throughput with isolated capacity; Private gives you complete network control for compliance.

[02:20] Jordan: On the performance side we have batching, KV cache / prefix caching, and quantization recommendations that help reduce tokens and cost. For your 60 QPS, we may recommend dedicated capacity for the triage path if you need strict p95 latency. If 300ms p95 is strict, you might need pinned instances or a higher commit.

[02:52] Ethan: When you say 'KV cache' — sorry that term's new to some folks — is that like a prefix cache for repeated prompts? Does it preserve PHI?

[03:05] Jordan: Good question. It's a prefix / KV cache that stores model KV state to speed up repeated sequences; it doesn't store raw PM data in readable form. For PHI we recommend zero-persistence or encryption and scoped logs. We can run through exact retention settings.

[03:30] Priya: Can you confirm where logs live? And access controls — RBAC, SSO, integration with our IdP?

[03:42] Diego (CSM): Absolutely. We support SSO via SAML, role-based access, and audit logs. For logs and retention we can either keep them for the default retention window or set a custom retention for enterprise customers. We'll share the security pack after the call.

[04:00] Liam O'Connor: Onboarding-wise, what does the pilot look like day-to-day? How long to get something usable?

[04:12] Samira: Typical pilot timeline is 2-4 weeks for an initial integration: week 0-1 provisioning and sample prompts, week 2 run small user testing and perf baseline, week 3 iterate on prompts and quality, week 4 evaluate against success criteria. That said we'll flex to your schedule.

[04:35] Dr. Alicia: Success criteria for us: 25% decrease in documentation time on average clinician workflow, and no measurable drop in triage accuracy — we'll provide labeled prompt sets.

[04:52] Jordan: Great — we'll create an eval harness and help you run a small A/B with human review. Also recommend collecting a small prompt set (100-300 examples) to baseline quality and to monitor regressions.

[05:10] Ethan: On the technical side, are there SDKs? We primarily run Node and Python microservices.

[05:18] Jordan: Yes, we have SDKs and REST endpoints; we'll send quickstart snippets. For hosted API you call our endpoints over TLS with API key; for Dedicated/Private there's a different network setup and we coordinate with your infra team.

[05:35] Priya: If we go Private or Dedicated in our VPC, what's the networking model — does Redwood set up peering or do we run a customer-managed SAM? Also, any IP allowlist?

[05:48] Jordan: We support several models: AWS VPC peering, PrivateLink, or an on-prem appliance for air-gapped customers. For Dedicated we can do peering or PrivateLink; for Private deployments we work with your infra on a site-to-site or in-cluster deployment. There will be an allowlist and cert-based auth. We'll share the network diagram.

[06:15] Priya: Good. Also KMS — we need to use our KMS for E2E encryption.

[06:22] Samira: That's supported. We integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private/Dedicated, and for hosted we have envelope encryption and optional BYOK for enterprise. We'll include the KMS integration notes.

[06:38] Ethan: About cost — can you outline the pricing models and committed capacity? If we do Dedicated, what's lock-in?

[06:47] Samira: Pricing: hosted API is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with monthly/annual commit; Private is enterprise licensing. For Dedicated there's a commit for capacity but you can configure autoscaling and burst; we can model cost versus p95 targets. We'll send a pricing spreadsheet.

[07:10] Liam: Any competitors considerations we should be aware of? We're evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI too.

[07:18] Diego: Totally normal. The differences usually come down to latency economics, model accuracy on your prompts, and enterprise controls. We'll help by running a small benchmark if you want apples-to-apples.

[07:33] Dr. Alicia: That benchmark would be helpful. We'd want to include accuracy on clinical notes and hallucination rate.

[07:40] Jordan: We'll include hallucination/precision metrics in the eval and a latency/cost comparison. For clinical contexts we often recommend smaller context-window models with stronger instruction tuning, then tune prompts.

[07:58] Ethan: On data handling — if clinicians paste PHI in prompts, is that retained in logs? Can you scrub it?

[08:07] Priya: Yes this is critical.

[08:10] Jordan: By default logs are retained for X days (we'll provide exact), but for pilot we can set retention to zero and disable logging, or redact PII. We'll put that in docs.

[08:25] Samira: We'll also share the security pack including SOC2 type II, penetration test summaries, and our encryption approach.

[08:35] Dr. Alicia: Timeline wise — we want to kickoff technical work this week and start pilot integration by next Monday. Is that feasible?

[08:44] Samira: Yes. Diego will provision the sandbox right after this call and Jordan will follow up with the SE deep-dive to get API keys and run perf tests.

[08:55] Diego: I'll create the sandbox and send API keys to Ethan and Jordan. Also scheduling weekly 30-min check-ins — propose Tuesdays at 10am PT.

[09:10] Ethan: That works.

[09:15] Priya: One more compliance ask: can Redwood sign a BAA? We handle PHI, so need to confirm legal.

[09:25] Samira: We have a BAA template for enterprise customers; legal will loop in. I'll attach the BAA and procurement flow in the follow-up.

[09:34] Liam: For success criteria, who will be the day-to-day contacts?

[09:40] Dr. Alicia: Ethan will own engineering; Priya for security; Liam for product.

[09:46] Samira: Great — to recap next steps: Samira shares onboarding packet + security docs; Diego provisions sandbox and sends API keys; Jordan schedules deep-dive and perf tests; Priya sends SOC2 / compliance items; customer confirms pilot scope by end of week.

[10:10] Ethan: Quick technical clarifying Q: what telemetry will we get — per-route token breakdown and per-request latencies?

[10:20] Jordan: Yes, the Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, traces and error rates. We'll share a sample dashboard export.

[10:34] Priya: Any special network ports or firewall rules we need to open?

[10:40] Jordan: For hosted it's standard HTTPS outbound. For Private/Dedicated there are additional ports for peerings and specific private endpoints; we'll include network config.

[10:52] Dr. Alicia: Okay sounds good.

[11:00] Samira: One last note: we'll run a small baseline test to verify p95 numbers. If the p95 is higher than target, options are increase commit, tune batching, or adjust model variant.

[11:20] Ethan: Understood.

[11:25] Diego: I'll capture action items and send calendar invites for the weekly sync.

[11:35] Liam: Thank you everyone.

[11:40] Samira: Thanks all — we'll follow up within 24 hours with the onboarding packet and security artifacts.

[11:50] (meeting ends)
